drills.stem: You need the minimum equipment grounding conductor (EGC) for a branch circuit protected by a 20A OCPD. What is the correct sizing METHOD?
choices: Size the EGC from Table 250.122 using the rating of the OCPD (20A)
Size the EGC from Table 250.66 using the service-entrance conductor
Match the EGC to the ungrounded conductor's ampacity in Table 310.16
Use the grounding electrode conductor rule in 250.66
hintLadder: Primary noun: equipment grounding conductor (EGC), the wire being sized, not the OCPD or the circuit conductors
Cite: Table 250.122, keyed to the OCPD rating. Read the size from your book

drills.stem: For a service, you must size the grounding ELECTRODE conductor (GEC). Which rule and INPUT govern that size?
choices: Table 250.122, keyed to the OCPD rating
250.66 (Table 250.66), keyed to the largest ungrounded service-entrance conductor
250.122(B), keyed to the upsized ungrounded conductor
hintLadder: Primary noun: grounding ELECTRODE conductor (GEC), a different conductor than the EGC
Tab family: 250 Grounding (the GEC lives at 250.66, not 250.122)
Cite: 250.66 / Table 250.66, sized from the service-entrance conductor. Read the value in your book

drills.stem: EGC vs GEC: which statement pairs each conductor with the correct sizing INPUT?
choices: Both are sized from the OCPD rating in Table 250.122
The EGC is sized from the OCPD (Table 250.122). The GEC is sized from the service conductor (250.66)
The EGC is sized from the service conductor (250.66). The GEC is sized from the OCPD (Table 250.122)
Both are sized from the ungrounded conductor ampacity in Table 310.16
hintLadder: Primary nouns: two different conductors, equipment grounding conductor and grounding electrode conductor
Tab families: 250.122 EGC for the EGC, 250 Grounding for the GEC
Cite: EGC = Table 250.122 (OCPD input). GEC = 250.66 (service-conductor input). Confirm both in your book
